commits.summary: Stub reachability, step 1: an experiment job that has JBMC's solver decide whether VF-015's proof enters the String.format stub (verification pending)
commits.body:
llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md's step 1. The gap preflight counts a stub as entered when JBMC's symbolic execution alone keeps a step of it. For VF-015's proof (prove Hex#toDigit --assume 'ch == 1632' on commons-codec's old Hex), that counts String.format(String, Object[]) as entered on toDigit's exception path, which the assumption makes infeasible. The new verification/triage/stub-reachability.sh reruns that proof unchanged, with JBMC behind a wrapper that records each command and its time. On the proof's harness and command it then tries two methods. (A) --cover location in place of --unwinding-assertions, reading the goals of DecoderException's constructor, of the stub and of toDigit, and once more with --property on one goal. (B) The proof as given, with a rewritten DecoderException whose String.format call first calls a probe that fails an assertion of its own (throw new AssertionError(), as GapIntrinsics.open). Both also run on a control, the same prove without --assume, where the call is reachable. The job's description gives the outcome each method is expected to have.

Checked inline: the script's syntax, its argv rewriting on made-up commands, and its recording wrapper with echo in place of JBMC. No JBMC was run. The brief's Progress records why the probe is a rewritten caller and not a rewritten goto program: jbmc 6.11 can't write a goto binary for goto-instrument. jbmc --help lists --cover only in --unwinding-assertions' line, so whether --cover is accepted is for the job to show.

Verification pending: job 20261107-233000-stub-reachability-step-1-can-jbmc-s-solv (verification/jobs/). Step 2, choosing the method, waits on its result.

commits.summary: Stub reachability, step 2: the probe at the call site is chosen, since JBMC 6.11 has no --cover
commits.body: The step 1 job (20261107-233000-stub-reachability-step-1-can-jbmc-s-solv) passed. It reproduced VF-015's step 3 on commons-codec 87f6aa28 and a control without the --assume, then tried two ways of having JBMC's solver decide whether the proof reaches String.format's stub. --cover location is a usage error: JBMC 6.11 doesn't know the option, and the brief's claim that it has one is wrong (the mention in --unwinding-assertions' help line is CBMC's text). A probe assertion at DecoderException's String.format call, from a rewritten caller, was correct on both: it holds under ch == 1632 and fails without the assumption. It took 92 ms, against the proof's 129 ms. llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md's Progress records the measurements and the choice. It also records what step 3 must keep: the probe counts only when the run's unwinding assertions hold; a probe that throws ends its path, so stubs are probed one per run or the probe is guarded by a nondet branch; and a stub leaves the gaps only when every one of its call sites' probes holds. Verified by reading the job's log and outputs; nothing else changed.

commits.summary: Stub reachability, step 3: the gap preflight asks JBMC's solver, by a probe at each call site, whether a path reaches a stub its symbolic execution enters
commits.body:
llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md's step 3. JBMC's symbolic execution keeps a branch whose condition only a solver decides, so the gap preflight counted a stub behind an --assume as entered. That is VF-015's case: String.format on toDigit's exception path, which ch == 1632 closes. Now, for the stubs symbolic execution still enters, the preflight in lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs runs the proof once more, with its bounds and solver, over every input. Each call site of those stubs (the goto listing's bytecode-index, and the instruction there must call the stub) is rewritten to a method of jvmcontract.StubProbe. Behind CProver.nondetBoolean() that method fails an assertion of its own, and otherwise it makes the call, so no path is cut. The rewrite uses a new shared::redirect_calls_at, which also passes the call site's place. A stub leaves the gaps only when all of its probes hold and so does every unwinding assertion. It joins Found::unreached and the new Found::solved, and the note names why. The stub stays a gap when the run is out of time, gives no verdict or can't be read, or when a call site can't be probed. Preflight::probes records the run. The module doc, lib/README.md's gap section and Preflight::paths' doc describe it.

Verified inline. There are unit tests on step 2's recorded probe output for VF-015's case, which reads as unreached. Its variants don't: the control, a missing probe, one failing probe of two, a failing unwinding assertion, no verdict, a timeout. A placement test covers two stubs in sequence, a call site whose instruction calls another method, and one with no bytecode index. Another test checks the gaps and the note. The live reproducer, a_stub_behind_a_condition_only_the_solver_decides_is_no_gap, is a millisecond JBMC run on the new P.sequenced, like the existing fixture tests. It fails with the third step reduced to a no-op (the old behaviour) and passes with it. Its output shows the second of two stubs in sequence still reached past the first's probe, and confirms that JBMC lowers throw new AssertionError() to an assertion and assume(false), which step 2 only remembered. The unit suite passes (215), and all targets compile. The integration and conformance gap tests, which run JBMC proofs, are step 4's guard job.

The second, 20261108-011441-stub-reachability-step-4-no-stub-a-proof, guards that the probe leaves out no stub a proof does enter. It runs the jbmc_gaps unit tests (live ones included) on the runner's JBMC, the eight gap tests in lib/tests/integration.rs (the filters were checked inline with --list), and the conformance corpus under --engine jbmc and auto, all unchanged. commits.summary: Stub reachability, step 4 done: the guard passed, and VF-015 is deferred by the timebox on an uncaught checked exception in the equivalence harness
commits.body:
Both of step 4's jobs were collected in pktlkzsp. The guard job, 20261108-011441-stub-reachability-step-4-no-stub-a-proof, passed: the gap preflight's unit tests, the eight gap tests in lib/tests/integration.rs, and the conformance corpus under --engine jbmc and auto. So the probe leaves out no stub a proof enters. VF-015's job, 20261108-011411-vf-015-example-109-revisited-hex-todigit, now passes the step this brief targets. Step 3, the old toDigit under --assume 'ch == 1632', is proved under --gaps strict, and its note names String.format as a stub the solver shows unreached. But the job fails at step 5, the ASCII equivalence, with 'an unexpected property failed: EquivalenceHarness.check:(CI)V.1'.

Triaged from the job's JBMC traces (work-change and work-ascii jbmc.log). The property is JBMC's 'no uncaught exception'. The old toDigit throws DecoderException on a non-hex ASCII char (ch = 0). That exception is checked, and the equivalence harness's call handlers (harness::EXCEPTIONS in lib/src/harness/mod.rs) catch only unchecked exceptions and Error. Step 4's 'test $? -eq 1' also accepted that 'cannot be verified', so its pass shows nothing. The throwing-initializer notes suspected when the result was collected are not the cause. This is N3's second failure in a row, so VF-015 is deferred by the timebox. The fix is outside this brief's stub gaps: the harness would need to tell declared exceptions apart, and the job's step 4 would need to check for a found change. Progress, VF-015's entry in verification/findings.md and example 109's notes record the finding and what a further attempt costs. Step 4's criterion is met, so Progress ends with Status: done. Nothing here needed a run: the triage read collected logs.

The brief's plan expected VF-015's next failure, if any, to be the StandardCharsets.UTF_8 replay (lib/src/interp/natives.rs:373). It wasn't: the replay never came up. That expectation is out of date.

commits.summary: application-core: the user's decisions settled, and VF-015 brought in scope as Phase 0's step 7
commits.body:
The user settled the brief's six proposed decisions as drafted: the four streams as scoped, with optional work never blocking a row; verification with the pipeline; one writer for shared files; Phase 0 in the planning session; 4 GB per stream and about 24 GB for the runner; claude-opus-5-5 at high effort. They added a seventh: VF-015 is in scope. The stub-reachability loop's timebox deferred VF-015 to a person on 2026-11-08, after finding its cause: the equivalence harness's call handlers (harness::EXCEPTIONS) catch only unchecked exceptions and Error, so commons-codec's checked DecoderException leaves EquivalenceHarness.check uncaught, and no equivalence over a method that throws a checked exception can be verified.

It goes in Phase 0, not a stream: the fix is in harness/, the objects stream's file; the environment stream's E2 (modelled failures, catch and propagation) needs it; and it is small. Step 7 has a reproducer first. The handlers then catch each class in either version's throws clause, then java.lang.Exception, comparing by class, and a checked exception that only one version throws is refuted. The closing job is VF-015's resubmitted with step 4 made stricter: the change must be found with its witness replayed, where test $? -eq 1 also accepted 'cannot be verified'. It has no timebox attempt left, so a failure goes back to the user. The starting-point table, prerequisites 1 and 5, Phase 0's Done-when row and Progress are updated, and E2's brief points at step 7. The status stays blocked on Phase 0.
